note: ہوں is the first-person singular present form of ہونا and should give the direct learner gloss 'am' rather than only grammatical metadata.

proposed_english: country; land; state/realm; property/possession (مِلْک, different vocalization)

note: بات commonly means talk/conversation as well as thing, point, matter, or saying. The conversational sense is too basic to omit.
proposed_english: talk; conversation; thing; point; matter; saying

note: طرح centrally means way/manner/method/type/kind. 'Condition' is not an appropriate core learner gloss here.
دو is both the numeral two and the very common informal imperative of دینا: 'give!'. Numeral-only treatment hides a major homograph.
ہوا is the noun air/wind/breeze and also the masculine singular perfect form of ہونا meaning happened/became/was. Verb POS is listed but the verb meaning is missing.
proposed_english: air; wind; breeze; happened; became; was (masculine singular form of ہونا)

note: دی is the feminine singular perfect form of دینا ('gave'). 'Content word' is not an adequate learner POS.
حاصل has noun uses such as result/outcome and adjectival/participial uses such as obtained/acquired. Adjective-only POS contradicts the noun meanings already listed.
سی is a resemblance/comparative element meaning like/as/-like, especially the feminine form. 'Closed-class' is too vague for learner grammar.
پہلے is very commonly an adverb meaning before/earlier/previously as well as an inflected form related to پہلا 'first'. Adjective-only POS is incomplete.
کچھ means some but also something, a little, and in context any. A one-word gloss is too narrow for this high-frequency item.
صرف centrally means only/just/solely. 'Busy' is incorrect dictionary noise; noun uses such as expenditure/spending and morphology are specialized secondary senses.
proposed_english: only; just; solely; expenditure/spending; morphology (grammar, specialized)

note: سال is the ordinary Urdu noun 'year'. 'Hall' and 'house' are spurious cross-language/dictionary noise in this learner entry.
لیے most commonly occurs in کے لیے 'for', but it is also a plural/oblique perfect form of لینا meaning taken. Verb-only POS does not account for the compound-postposition use.
proposed_english: for; for the sake of (in کے لیے); taken (form of لینا, context-dependent)

note: اسی is a major homograph: it can mean eighty (assī) or 'this/that very; the same' (isī). The current entry teaches only the numeral and misses the extremely common pronominal/emphatic use.
proposed_english: eighty; this very; that very; the same (context-dependent)

note: خلاف is commonly used in کے خلاف 'against' and also means opposition/contrary. Adjective-only POS is too narrow.
proposed_english: against; contrary to; opposed to; opposition

note: افراد is the plural of فرد and means individuals/persons/members. The current gloss 'kinds, types, species' is incorrect.
جن is commonly the plural oblique relative pronoun 'whom/which/those who'; the same spelling can also denote jinn. Noun-only POS hides the dominant grammatical use.
proposed_english: whom; which; those who (plural oblique relative pronoun); jinn (noun, context-dependent)

note: آ is the verb stem/imperative of آنا meaning come/come!, not merely a 'character'.
